Date: 2027-05-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: QBR prep: infra scaling & unit economics — kickoff

Team — kicking off a short working thread to capture decisions and owners for the QBR infra segment (focus: GPU spend runway, utilization targets, batching/caching tradeoffs). Goal: surface the 3 asks we present to Exec on 5/10 and be explicit about actions required to hit the OKR check-in.

High-level context:
- Current committed GPU monthly spend: $1.8M (on-reserve + burst).
- Last-week utilization (p95 across fleet): 62%; peanut-burst spikes to 93% on training/large evals.
- Recent batching work dropped per-token CPU overhead by ~11% in experiments but increased 95th p95 latency by ~40ms for short seqs.

Immediate asks (please own by EOD Wed):
1) Lauren — compile a 2-slide exec summary showing spend run-rate, committed vs burst, and 3 scenarios (conservative / base / aggressive) for Q3 capacity. Attachments: initial-runbook.xlsx + utilization-snapshot.csv.
2) Marissa — model-level unit economics: top 6 serving models; show token cost delta across quantization & batching regimes. Put rough $/1M tokens numbers next to each.
3) Karthik — run a prioritized experiment matrix for batching thresholds and KV cache hit-rate targets that preserve 99th pct latency SLO. Add a short risk note for fallback policies.

Notes: I invited Pegasus infra (infra-team@pegasus.ai) to comment on burst capacity SLAs — they may respond in-thread. Also flagged Kathy from Borealis (procurement) to pre-check discount cadence if we need to increase reserved commits.

Attachments: [Attachment: initial-runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)], [Attachment: utilization-snapshot.csv (csv)]

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee

Soojin — thanks for the kickoff. I'm drafting the 2 slides; a few clarifying asks so the scenarios are defensible: 

- Definition check: base scenario = maintain current reserved commit + moderate batching gains (10% token cost reduction). Conservative = defer new reserves, rely on burst (higher $/token). Aggressive = additional reserved commit to shave $/token by 22% (includes expected QoS downgrade risk). Agree?
- For the slides I want: current committed v CPU/GPU split, list of mapped services consuming top 70% of GPU minutes, and a short note on fallback chain (model-variant routing -> region failover -> burst pool).

Pegasus: can you confirm burst pool headroom assumptions for June (percent available under 24h notice)?

I'll attach the exec slide drafts by EOD Tue.

Lauren/Soojin — quick note from Pegasus infra: expected burst headroom for June under 24h notice is ~18-22% of today's total on the cluster you typically use (region-us-west-2). We can push to 30% with 72h lead time but that requires temporary capacity shift that impacts maintenance windows.

If you plan to rely on burst for the conservative scenario, expect a 1.4x price-on-burst multiplier for sustained 12h windows. Happy to provide more granular per-instance type numbers if you share the runbook slice.

—Alex, Pegasus Capacity Planning
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

On Sun, May 2, 2027 at 12:27 PM, infra-team@pegasus.ai wrote:
> Lauren/Soojin — quick note from Pegasus infra: expected burst headroom for June under 24h notice is ~18-22% ...

Thanks Alex — useful. Team, preliminary model-level numbers, very rough (see below). I ran a 72h sim with current traffic traces + two batching profiles: conservative batching (batch windows <=20ms) and aggressive batching (windows up to 80ms). Key takeaways: 

- Top 6 models (by cost): chat-xl, instruct-13B, summarizer-6B, reranker-3B, embed-2B, safety-filter.
- Per 1M tokens served (base quant/short seq): chat-xl = $66, instruct-13B = $41, summarizer-6B = $18. With conservative batching: -9% average token cost; aggressive batching: -22% cost but 95th-latency risk rises for sub-128 seqs by ~55ms.
- KV cache: raising local KV cache hit from 45% -> 70% reduces per-token cost by ~7% and p95 latency for long seqs improves ~35ms. Cache warmup and eviction policy complexity increases engineering effort by ~2-3 sprint-weeks.

Asks: 
1) Decision for Exec: do we present aggressive batching as an achievable 90-day play (with a clear risk mitigation plan) or relegate it to an experiment lane?
2) Approval to include a proposal to increase reserved commits by 15% for Q3 if we verify >15% aggregate cost savings across top 3 models.

Attaching: [Attachment: batching-profiles.pdf (pdf)], [Attachment: cache-latency-tests.zip (zip)]

-Marissa
Head of Platform Costing
Redwood Inference

I'll consolidate into one slide appendix once I have Marissa's numbers.
